title: Stack of plates
prompt:
Four plates go into `main`'s stack frame, the space on the stack it sets aside for itself, and they come back out top-first. The starter reads the plates one at a time into `plate_r`; each read overwrites the plate before it, so store every plate in its named stack slot before the next read comes in. Then load them back and print them in reverse order.

The starter already sizes the frame, rounded up to a multiple of 16, and gives each slot a named offset. Your job is the `str`s going in and the `ldr`s coming out; the printing order is what makes it a stack.

## what is checked

- four lines, `89`, `55`, `34`, `21`, for the plates in the stdin box
- the program exits cleanly
- the plates go into the frame with `str`
- the same holds for other plates you do not see, zeros and the largest and smallest 64-bit values among them
starter:
// store four plates in the frame, then take them back top-first
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(plate_r, x19)

p1_s = 16                                   // bottom plate's offset
p2_s = 24
p3_s = 32
p4_s = 40                                   // top plate's offset
alloc = -(16 + 32) & -16
dealloc = -alloc

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld"
fmt_out:    .string "%lld\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
plate_m:    .skip 8

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, alloc]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // plate 1, the bottom one
        ldr     x1, =plate_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =plate_m
        ldr     plate_r, [x9]
        // TODO: store plate_r in its slot, [fp, p1_s]

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // plate 2
        ldr     x1, =plate_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =plate_m
        ldr     plate_r, [x9]
        // TODO: store plate_r in [fp, p2_s]

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // plate 3
        ldr     x1, =plate_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =plate_m
        ldr     plate_r, [x9]
        // TODO: store plate_r in [fp, p3_s]

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // plate 4, the top one
        ldr     x1, =plate_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =plate_m
        ldr     plate_r, [x9]
        // TODO: store plate_r in [fp, p4_s]

        // TODO: load the plates back top-first, from [fp, p4_s] down to
        // [fp, p1_s], and print each one with fmt_out.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], dealloc
        ret
